Contributing to z3r

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

Bug reports and pull requests are welcome at https://github.com/adamrsophie/z3r/issues.

Reporting a bug

Please include:

  • the output of z3r::z3_version() and sessionInfo();
  • a minimal example, ideally with the SMT-LIB2 text from z3_to_smtlib();
  • for a wrong answer, what the z3 command-line tool returns for the same SMT-LIB2 text.

Development setup

  1. Install Z3 with its headers (see the README).
  2. Install the development dependencies: install.packages(c("Rcpp", "roxygen2", "testthat", "gmp", "knitr", "rmarkdown")).
  3. After editing C++ export annotations or roxygen comments, run Rcpp::compileAttributes() and roxygen2::roxygenise().
  4. Run R CMD build . and R CMD check --as-cran z3r_*.tar.gz.

Rules for native code

  • Every Z3 handle is held through z3r::Ref<T> (see src/z3r.h), which takes a reference on construction and releases it on destruction, and keeps the context alive.
  • Check the Z3 error state after every call that can fail (own(), own_ast() and check() do this) before using the result.
  • Do the sort checking in z3r. Z3’s C API silently coerces some ill-sorted terms, for example Booleans in arithmetic.
  • Never call R from a thread other than the main thread, and never use a Z3 context from two threads.

Tests

Tests should check mathematical results, not only that calls succeed. Where possible compare with an independent route: brute force over a small domain, R’s own arithmetic, or the z3 command-line tool on exported SMT-LIB2.
